They were originally presented as strange boys with long hair wearing trenchcoats. In Generation III, they were changed to ers dressing up in Pokémon-like costumes. In Generation VII, Poké Maniacs cosplay as and, when defeated, imitate Slowpoke with their faces. They are named for their enthusiasm for " "-esque Pokémon, and tend to use Pokémon in the , such as , , and .

plainText:
A Poké Maniac (Japanese: かいじゅうマニア Maniac; also known as マニア Maniac in Generation I), formatted Pokémaniac in Generations I to III, is a type of Pokémon Trainer that first debuted in the Generation I games. They were originally presented as strange boys with long hair wearing trenchcoats. In Generation III, they were changed to ers dressing up in Pokémon-like costumes. In Generation VII, Poké Maniacs cosplay as and, when defeated, imitate Slowpoke with their faces. They are named for their enthusiasm for " "-esque Pokémon, and tend to use Pokémon in the , such as , , and .

In Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, Poké Maniacs will award three s along with prize money upon being defeated.

==Terminology==
In Generations I to III, this Trainer class is referred to as POKéMANIAC. In guidebooks, which often present these names in sentence case, it is often formatted as Pokémaniac .

From Generation IV onward, this Trainer class is named Poké Maniac.

==Notable Poké Maniacs==
In , Kirk (known as Mania in Generation II), a Poké Maniac from Cianwood City, is well known for his arrogance. Hearing of this, stole one of his two Pokémon, a . Kirk begs the player to take Shuckie, his , for safekeeping. Depending on how well Shuckie is treated, Kirk may or may not ask for Shuckie to be given back.

Aside from the Trainer class, the term Poké Maniac (Japanese: ポケモンマニア Pokémon Maniac) has also been used to refer to people that are deeply interested in rare Pokémon, most notably Bill and his father. However, in original Japanese version, this term is different from the class and does not carry the implication of liking Kaiju-like Pokémon. Probably for this reason, Bill's title was re-translated to Pokémon fanatic in the English version of Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!.

==Trivia==
The Poké Maniacs in wear black shirts with the Pokéstar Studios logo.
The official Pokémon Youtube channel posted a music video featuring Poké Maniac in 2018. 
Hayata and Riku, the Poké Maniacs served as narrators on the Pokémon Daisuki Club website in 2018, are presumed references to the respective human protagonists from and .
